news_analysis.headline_hook: Your ₹1,000 SIP didn't make ₹4.67 Lakh. Fees and taxes took their cut first.
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: Livemint reported that a ₹1,000 monthly SIP in a specific diversified equity mutual fund grew to ₹4.67 lakh over a 10-year period.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors assume that picking the 'top-performing' fund from a 10-year retrospective list guarantees similar future wealth creation, ignoring survivorship bias and the reality of mean reversion.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: The reported returns are heavily skewed by the bull market cycle of the last decade; institutions know that 'top-performing' funds often suffer from asset bloat, leading to 'closet indexing' where the fund manager stops taking active risks to protect their AUM-based fee structure.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never select a fund based on trailing 10-year absolute returns; instead, evaluate the fund's rolling returns and downside capture ratio to ensure the manager isn't just riding a market beta wave.

carousel_outline.focus: Why the '₹4.67 Lakh SIP' headline is a dangerous trap for your retirement planning.

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: Past 10-year returns are a reliable predictor of future fund performance.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: Retrospective returns are often skewed by bull market cycles and survivorship bias, ignoring funds that failed or merged.

slides.title: The Hidden Cost of Asset Bloat

stat_data.label: estimated performance drag
stat_data.context: As AUM swells, managers shift to 'closet indexing' to protect fees. This reduces active alpha, effectively costing investors significant potential gains compared to a low-cost index tracker.

slides.title: The Institutional Liquidity Trap
flowchart_data: 1. Fund hits 'top performer' status, attracting massive retail inflows.
2. Manager struggles to deploy capital efficiently due to size constraints.
3. Strategy shifts from active alpha generation to defensive, index-hugging behavior.

slides.title: Mathematical Drag: The Silent Extractor
slides.card_text: When a fund grows too large, the manager's priority shifts from beating the benchmark to minimizing tracking error. You end up paying active management fees for passive index-like returns, creating a permanent drag on your compounding engine.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Institutional Rule
slides.card_text: Never select a fund based on trailing 10-year absolute returns. Instead, evaluate the fund's rolling returns and downside capture ratio. This ensures the manager is delivering genuine alpha rather than just riding a market beta wave.
